q.s: The National e-Governance Service Delivery Assessment (NeSDA), which assesses the e-governance services of States, was introduced by which body in 2019?
q.x: NeSDA was introduced in 2019 by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG).

q.s: The head office of the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG), upgraded from the National Institute of Administrative Research, is located at:
q.x: The NCGG has its head office in New Delhi and a branch at Mussoorie.

q.s: The term 'good governance' was brought into development discourse by the World Bank in its 1989 report on:
q.x: The World Bank's 1989 report on Sub-Saharan Africa first used 'good governance' in development discourse.

q.s: Which of the following statements about governance is correct?
o: Governance includes markets and civil society along with the State.
Governance has no link with citizen participation.
q.x: Governance is wider than government, covering the State, markets and civil society.

q.s: According to UNDP, the three most critical characteristics of good governance are transparency, accountability and:
q.x: UNDP names transparency, accountability and responsiveness as the three most critical characteristics.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the eight attributes of good governance listed by the UN/UNDP?
q.x: The eight attributes include participation, rule of law, transparency, responsiveness, consensus orientation, equity, effectiveness and accountability; centralisation is not one of them.

q.s: The Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI), compiled since 1996 for over 200 countries, are published by:
q.x: The WGI are a World Bank product covering over 200 countries since 1996.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six dimensions of the World Bank's Worldwide Governance Indicators?
q.x: The HDI is a UNDP index, not a WGI dimension.

q.s: The Grievance Redressal Assessment and Index (GRAI), which ranks Union ministries on handling public grievances, is published by:
q.x: GRAI is published by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances.

q.s: Which State topped NITI Aayog's Investment Friendliness Index 2026?
q.x: Gujarat topped the Investment Friendliness Index 2026.

q.s: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission, set up in 2005, submitted how many reports?
q.x: The Second ARC (2005) submitted 15 reports.

q.s: The 12th Report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission is titled:
o: Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance
q.x: The 12th Report is 'Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance'; 'Ethics in Governance' was the 4th Report (2007).

q.s: Under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, registering a trade union requires a minimum of:
o: 15% of workers or 150 workers, whichever is more
10% of workers or 100 workers, whichever is less
q.x: The Code requires 10% of workers or 100 workers, whichever is less.

q.s: APCOS, set up by Andhra Pradesh in 2020, was created to:
o: Recruit outsourced staff and pay them directly
q.x: The AP Corporation for Outsourced Services recruits outsourced staff and pays them directly, cutting out contractors.

q.s: The Civil Services Board in Andhra Pradesh is mainly meant to:
o: Curb political interference in postings and transfers
q.x: Civil Services Boards are intended to insulate postings and transfers from political interference.

q.s: The first lateral-entry Joint Secretaries joined the Union government in the year:
q.x: The first lateral-entry Joint Secretaries joined in 2019.

q.s: Which body recommended lateral entry into the Union government at the Joint Secretary level?
q.x: The Second ARC recommended lateral entry at the Joint Secretary level.

q.s: The Seventh Central Pay Commission, which submitted its report in 2015, was chaired by:
q.x: Justice A.K. Mathur chaired the Seventh CPC; Justice B.N. Srikrishna chaired the Sixth.

q.s: The Sixth Central Pay Commission was chaired by:
q.x: Justice B.N. Srikrishna chaired the Sixth CPC; Justice S. Ratnavel Pandian chaired the Fifth.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT usually listed among the pioneers of New Public Management?
q.x: The UK under Thatcher, New Zealand, Australia and the USA are the NPM pioneers.

q.s: The term 'New Public Management' was popularised in 1991 by:
q.x: Christopher Hood popularised the term NPM in 1991; Osborne and Gaebler wrote 'Reinventing Government' (1992).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of New Public Management?
q.x: NPM stresses output controls rather than input controls.

q.s: The 'New Public Service' approach (2000), which treats people as citizens rather than customers, was propounded by:
q.x: Robert and Janet Denhardt propounded the New Public Service (2000).

q.s: The concept of 'Creating Public Value' (1995) in public administration is associated with:
q.x: Mark Moore's 'Creating Public Value' (1995) holds that public value includes legitimacy and trust, not efficiency alone.

q.s: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) was set up on 1 October 2007 under the:
q.x: PNGRB was set up under the PNGRB Act, 2006.

q.s: The chairperson of a sectoral regulator such as TRAI or CCI can be removed by:
o: The Central Government on grounds stated in the Act
The President on the advice of the Supreme Court only
q.x: Chairpersons are removed by the Central Government on statutory grounds (insolvency, moral turpitude, incapacity, abuse of position) after a hearing.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that High Court judicial review over tribunals is part of the basic structure?
q.x: L. Chandra Kumar (1997) restored High Court review of tribunal decisions as part of the basic structure.

q.s: The Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) was set up in the year:
q.x: APTEL was set up on 24 August 2004 under the Electricity Act, 2003.

q.s: The theory of 'regulatory capture', under which a regulator ends up serving the industry it regulates, was put forward by:
q.x: George Stigler put forward regulatory capture theory in 1971.

q.s: Annual reports and accounts of regulators laid before Parliament are mainly examined by:
q.x: Regulators' reports are examined by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees.

q.s: Which of the following statements about regulatory governance is correct?
o: Unrestricted removal of members by the parent ministry strengthens a regulator's independence.
Regulators are not answerable to Parliament in any form.
Regulators' annual reports are examined only by the Public Accounts Committee.
The Economic Survey 2025-26 says sanctions should be proportional to intent, scale and harm.
q.x: The Survey calls for proportionate sanctions; unrestricted removal weakens independence, and reports go to the DRSCs.

q.s: The ordinance of 18 June 2010 that resolved the ULIP dispute between SEBI and IRDA placed ULIPs under:
q.x: The ordinance placed ULIPs under IRDA and created a joint mechanism chaired by the Finance Minister.

q.s: The Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission (FSLRC) was headed by:
q.x: Justice B.N. Srikrishna headed the FSLRC.

q.s: The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan (VBSA) Bill, 2025 proposes a single higher-education regulator replacing:
q.x: The VBSA Bill, 2025 proposes one regulator replacing UGC, AICTE and NCTE.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Single Desk Portal, launched in April 2015, promises industrial clearances within:
q.x: The AP Single Desk Portal promises clearances within 21 working days.

q.s: The National Policy on the Voluntary Sector, 2007 was brought out by:
q.x: It was brought out by the Planning Commission; NITI Aayog was set up only in 2015.

q.s: Civil society is often called the 'third sector' because it stands beside:
q.x: Civil society is the third sector beside the State (first) and the market (second).

q.s: The present Press Council of India is a statutory, quasi-judicial body constituted under the:
o: Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867
q.x: The present PCI functions under the Press Council Act, 1978; the first PCI (1966) was under the 1965 Act.

q.s: Which of the following actions can the Press Council of India NOT take against a newspaper?
q.x: The PCI has no punitive powers; it can only warn, admonish or censure.

q.s: By convention, the Chairman of the Press Council of India is:
q.x: By custom the PCI Chairman is a retired Supreme Court judge, chosen by the Rajya Sabha Chairman, Lok Sabha Speaker and a Council member.

q.s: The FCRA amendment of 2020 reduced the ceiling on administrative expenses from foreign contributions to:
q.x: The 2020 amendment cut the cap from 50% to 20% and banned sub-granting.

q.s: The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) is administered by the:
q.x: The FCRA is administered by the Home Ministry; FEMA is administered by the RBI and ED.

q.s: Registration of an NGO under the FCRA is valid for a period of:
q.x: FCRA registration is valid for five years and must then be renewed.

q.s: Under the FCRA Amendment Rules, 2026, renewal of registration requires an NGO to have spent ₹10 lakh over a period of:
q.x: Renewal under the 2026 Rules needs ₹10 lakh spent over two years.

q.s: The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC), India's oldest central trade union, was founded in:
q.x: The AITUC was founded in 1920 (N.M. Joshi among its founders), before the Trade Unions Act, 1926.

q.s: Which central trade union is the labour wing of the Indian National Congress?
q.x: INTUC (1947) is the Congress's labour wing; BMS is linked to the Sangh Parivar.

q.s: Trade unions in India obtain legal recognition under the:
q.x: The Trade Unions Act, 1926 provides for registration and legal recognition of unions.

q.s: According to M. Laxmikanth, the most powerful pressure groups in India are:
o: Business groups such as FICCI, CII and ASSOCHAM
q.x: Laxmikanth ranks business groups as the most powerful pressure groups.

q.s: What is the number of the National Consumer Helpline in India?
q.x: The National Consumer Helpline is 1915; 1098 is Childline, 1930 is cybercrime, 112 is emergency.

q.s: 'Jagriti' is the mascot of which consumer awareness campaign?
q.x: Jagriti is the mascot of the Jago Grahak Jago campaign.

q.s: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 came into force on:
q.x: The CCPA came into force on 24 July 2020.

q.s: For a first misleading advertisement, the CCPA may impose a penalty on the manufacturer or endorser of up to:
q.x: The first-offence penalty is up to Rs 10 lakh; repeat offences attract up to Rs 50 lakh and a bar of up to three years for endorsers.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 is correct?
o: Its consumer mediation cells are attached to the High Courts.
It recognises only four consumer rights.
It replaced the Consumer Protection Act, 1986.
It does not cover e-commerce transactions.
q.x: The 2019 Act replaced the 1986 Act, recognises six rights and attaches mediation cells to the Consumer Commissions.

q.s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, if a Consumer Commission does not decide the admissibility of a complaint within 21 days, the complaint is:
q.x: A complaint is deemed admitted if admissibility is not decided within 21 days.

q.s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, which of the following is NOT a consumer?
o: A person who buys a television for home use
A person who hires a service for personal use
A person who buys goods for resale
A person who buys goods online for own use
q.x: A buyer for resale or commercial purpose is excluded from the definition of consumer.

q.s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, an appeal against a District Commission order lies to the State Commission within:
q.x: Appeals from the District to the State Commission lie within 45 days; from the State to the National Commission within 30 days.

q.s: The pecuniary jurisdiction of Consumer Commissions under the 2019 Act is decided by the:
o: Value of consideration paid for goods or services
q.x: Pecuniary jurisdiction depends on the value of consideration paid.

q.s: How many dark patterns are listed in the Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023?
q.x: The Dark Patterns Guidelines, 2023 list 13 dark patterns.

q.s: Under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, the grievance officer must acknowledge a consumer complaint within:
q.x: The complaint must be acknowledged within 48 hours and redressed within one month.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Cabinet Committee on Security?
q.x: The CCS has the PM and the Home, Defence, Finance and External Affairs Ministers.

q.s: Who is the ex officio President of the Indian Council of World Affairs (ICWA)?
q.x: The Vice-President is ex officio President of the ICWA.

q.s: India established full diplomatic relations with Israel in 1992 during the prime ministership of:
q.x: Full relations with Israel were established in 1992 under P.V. Narasimha Rao.

q.s: 'Half-Lion' is a book by Vinay Sitapati on:
q.x: 'Half-Lion: How P.V. Narasimha Rao Transformed India' is by Vinay Sitapati.

q.s: The Simla Agreement between India and Pakistan was signed in the year:
q.x: The Simla Agreement was signed in 1972; Tashkent was 1966 and the Lahore Declaration 1999.

q.s: Which of the following agreements was NOT signed between India and Pakistan?
q.x: The Farakka Accord (1977) was with Bangladesh on sharing Ganga waters.

q.s: The island of Katchatheevu was ceded by India to Sri Lanka in the year:
q.x: Katchatheevu was ceded to Sri Lanka in 1974.

q.s: The India-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987 was signed by Rajiv Gandhi and:
q.x: Rajiv Gandhi and J.R. Jayewardene signed the 1987 Accord.

q.s: During the Korean War, India headed the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission under:
q.x: Gen. K.S. Thimayya chaired the NNRC in Korea.

q.s: The foreign-policy doctrine of offering goodwill to neighbours without asking for reciprocity is known as the:
q.x: The Gujral Doctrine offered non-reciprocal goodwill to neighbours.

q.s: Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) pool which type of assets?
o: Infrastructure assets such as roads and power lines
q.x: InvITs pool infrastructure assets; REITs pool real-estate assets.

q.s: Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) in India are regulated by:
q.x: AIFs are regulated by SEBI under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT regulated by SEBI?
q.x: Insurance companies are regulated by IRDAI.

q.s: Investment in unlisted companies is classified as which type of financial instrument?
q.x: Investment in unlisted firms is private equity; hybrids include convertible preference shares and convertible debentures.

q.s: The CPSE ETF and Bharat-22 are examples of:
q.x: CPSE ETF and Bharat-22 are ETFs that trade on exchanges at prices close to their NAV.

q.s: The NIFTY 50 index of the National Stock Exchange is calculated by the:
q.x: NIFTY 50 uses the free-float market capitalisation method.

q.s: The NIFTY 50 index was launched on 22 April 1996 with a base value of:
q.x: The base is 3 November 1995 = 1000.

q.s: The Bombay Stock Exchange was set up in 1875 under the name:
o: Native Share and Stock Brokers' Association
q.x: The BSE began in 1875 as the Native Share and Stock Brokers' Association; NSE was set up in 1992.

q.s: Which was the first stock exchange in India to be recognised under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956?
q.x: BSE was the first exchange recognised under the SCRA, on 31 August 1957.

q.s: India INX, the international exchange at GIFT City, is regulated by:
q.x: Exchanges in GIFT City are regulated by the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA).

q.s: Which was India's first fully automated electronic stock exchange?
q.x: NSE was the first fully automated electronic exchange; BSE is Asia's oldest exchange.

q.s: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) was set up in November 1992 on the recommendation of the:
q.x: The NSE was set up on the Pherwani Committee's recommendation.

q.s: The first trading segment launched by the NSE in June 1994 was the:
q.x: NSE began with the Wholesale Debt Market in June 1994; the cash segment followed later.

q.s: SEBI requires arbitrage mutual funds to keep at least 65% of their investments in:
q.x: Arbitrage funds must keep at least 65% in equity.

q.s: In 2015 the Forward Markets Commission, the commodity futures regulator, was merged into:
q.x: The FMC was merged into SEBI in 2015.

q.s: India's first weather derivative, RAINMUMBAI, was launched by:
q.x: RAINMUMBAI was launched by NCDEX.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a primary-market transaction?
o: Buying existing shares on a stock exchange
q.x: Buying existing shares on an exchange is a secondary-market transaction; the primary market deals in new securities.

q.s: SME IPOs in India are listed on which separate platform of the NSE?
q.x: SME IPOs list on BSE SME and NSE Emerge.

q.s: India's first credit rating agency, set up in 1987, is:
q.x: CRISIL (1987) was India's first credit rating agency; ICRA followed in 1991.

q.s: The single-window system launched in 2025 for registration of Foreign Portfolio Investors is called:
q.x: FPIs register through the SWAGAT-FI single window (2025).

q.s: UTI, India's first mutual fund, was set up on 1 February 1964 under the:
q.x: UTI was set up under the UTI Act, 1963.

q.s: Which is India's largest mutual fund by assets under management today?
q.x: SBI Mutual Fund is the largest by AUM; UTI was only the first.

q.s: SEBI was first set up in 1988 as a non-statutory body and acquired statutory powers in the year:
q.x: SEBI got statutory status under the SEBI Act, 1992.

q.s: The parent law under which SEBI functions as a statutory body is the:
q.x: SEBI's parent law is the SEBI Act, 1992.

q.s: The Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) was set up in the year:
q.x: SAT came in 1995, after SEBI's statutory status (1992) and NSE's recognition (1993).

q.s: On getting statutory powers in 1992, SEBI took over the functions of the:
q.x: SEBI took over from the Controller of Capital Issues; the FMC merged into SEBI only in 2015.

q.s: Who took charge as Chairperson of SEBI in March 2025?
q.x: Tuhin Kanta Pandey became SEBI Chairperson in March 2025, succeeding Madhabi Puri Buch.

q.s: Under Section 4 of the SEBI Act, how many members of the SEBI Board are drawn from the Reserve Bank of India?
q.x: One member comes from the RBI; two are from the Finance and Law ministries.

q.s: The Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR), which replaced the Business Responsibility Report, is prescribed by:
q.x: The BRSR is prescribed by SEBI for listed companies.

q.s: SEBI introduced a verified 'tick mark' for registered broker apps in collaboration with:
q.x: The verified tick mark for broker apps was introduced with Google (Play Store).

q.s: The Securities Markets Code Bill, 2025 proposes to merge the SEBI Act 1992, the SCRA 1956 and the:
q.x: The Code merges the SEBI Act, the SCRA and the Depositories Act, 1996.

q.s: The Forward Markets Commission, which regulated commodity futures before merging with SEBI, was set up in:
q.x: The FMC was set up in 1953 and merged with SEBI in 2015.

q.s: An appeal against an order of the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) lies with the:
q.x: Appeals from SAT lie to the Supreme Court.

q.s: The Securities Appellate Tribunal was set up under which provision?
q.x: SAT was set up under Section 15K of the SEBI Act.

q.s: Which of the following statements about SEBI's powers is correct?
o: Inspection, search and seizure are its quasi-legislative powers.
Passing disgorgement orders is a quasi-judicial power.
q.x: Disgorgement orders are quasi-judicial; inspection, search and seizure are investigative powers.

q.s: The RBI Retail Direct Scheme allows retail investors to buy directly from the RBI:
q.x: Retail Direct is for G-Secs, not corporate bonds.

q.s: SEBI issued its regulations for Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and InvITs in the year:
q.x: SEBI's REIT and InvIT Regulations came in 2014.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an Andhra Pradesh item in the Thirteenth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Integrated steel plant in YSR (Kadapa) district
q.x: The Bayyaram (Khammam) steel plant was a Telangana item; Kadapa steel, Dugarajapatnam port and the refinery were for AP.

q.s: After the 14th Finance Commission, what was offered to Andhra Pradesh in 2016 instead of Special Category Status?
q.x: A Special Assistance Measure (2016) was offered in place of SCS, which was only an oral assurance by the then PM and not in the Act.

q.s: Which of the following central PSUs is located in Andhra Pradesh and NOT in Telangana after bifurcation?
q.x: Hindustan Shipyard is at Visakhapatnam; BHEL, ECIL and BDL are in Hyderabad.

q.s: Which company acquired the Krishnapatnam (2020) and Gangavaram (2021) ports of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Adani Ports acquired Krishnapatnam in 2020 and Gangavaram in 2021.

q.s: The coastline of Andhra Pradesh, about 1,053 km long, ranks which in India?
q.x: AP's coastline (about 1,053 km) is the third longest, after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a challenge to commerce in residual Andhra Pradesh after 2014?
o: Absence of a large metropolitan commercial centre
Corporate and bank headquarters based outside the State
A short coastline with few port sites
Loss of Hyderabad as the capital
q.x: AP's long coastline (about 1,053 km) is an advantage, not a challenge.

q.s: The greenfield crude oil refinery and petrochemical complex promised to Andhra Pradesh is listed in which part of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
q.x: It is a Thirteenth Schedule item (via Section 93); Section 94 deals with tax incentives and capital support.

q.s: An air mass that is warmer than the surface over which it moves (a 'w' type) tends to give:
q.x: Warm air over a colder surface is stable, giving fog and stratus; 'k' type air is unstable.

q.s: After the passage of a cold front in the Northern Hemisphere, which of the following does NOT happen?
o: Wind backing from north-west to south-west
q.x: After a cold front the wind veers from south-west to north-west; it does not back.

q.s: Which type of cyclone is formed along fronts?
q.x: Temperate (extra-tropical) cyclones form on fronts; tropical cyclones form within a single warm, moist air mass.

q.s: Which of the following statements about tropical cyclones is correct?
o: They develop within a single warm, moist air mass.
They are most common near the poles.
q.x: Tropical cyclones have no fronts; they grow within one warm, moist air mass over warm seas.

q.s: Along a warm front, the warm air:
o: Stays stationary beside the cold air
Rises gently over the cold air
q.x: The lighter warm air rides up over the cold air along a warm front.

q.s: Which of the following statements about fronts is correct?
o: Fronts form only in the tropics.
Warm air undercuts cold air along a warm front.
Frontogenesis needs diverging air of similar properties.
A stationary front can give cloud and rain for several days.
q.x: A stationary front can bring prolonged cloud and rain; frontogenesis needs converging air of contrasting properties.

q.s: Which continent has the highest rate of population growth?
q.x: Africa has the highest population growth; Asia is the densest continent.

q.s: Which is the most densely populated country in the world?
q.x: Monaco is the densest country; Mongolia is among the sparsest.

q.s: Asia accounts for about what share of the world's population?
q.x: Asia holds about 59% of world population; Africa has the second largest share.

q.s: About 90% of the world's people live in the:
q.x: About 90% of humanity lives in the Northern Hemisphere.

q.s: The 'population explosion' after the Industrial Revolution was mainly caused by:
o: A sharp rise in birth rates
A sharp fall in death rates
q.x: The explosion came because death rates fell sharply while birth rates stayed high.

q.s: World population rose from 5 billion to 6 billion in only about:
q.x: The rise from 5 to 6 billion took about 12 years, while the first billion took over a million years.

q.s: The World Urbanization Prospects report is published by:
q.x: The World Urbanization Prospects is published by UN DESA's Population Division.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT among the most urbanised regions of the world?
q.x: Northern America, Latin America and Europe are the most urbanised; Africa and Asia show the fastest urban growth.

q.s: Which country is the largest producer of natural rubber, producing about one-third of the world total?
q.x: Thailand produces about one-third of natural rubber, followed by Indonesia.

q.s: Which two countries together produce about half of the world's cocoa?
q.x: Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana produce about half of world cocoa.

q.s: Vulcanisation of rubber, discovered by Charles Goodyear in 1839, involves heating rubber with:
q.x: Vulcanisation is heating rubber with sulphur.

q.s: Coffee leaf rust, which ruined coffee cultivation in Sri Lanka from 1869, is caused by a:
q.x: Coffee leaf rust is caused by the fungus Hemileia vastatrix; Sri Lanka then shifted to tea.

q.s: Cocoa plantation agriculture is mainly associated with which region?
q.x: Cocoa plantations are associated with West Africa; plantation farming is a product of colonialism.

q.s: Which type of farming is typical of Monsoon Asia?
q.x: Monsoon Asia has intensive subsistence farming; mixed farming is typical of Europe and eastern North America.

q.s: The Masai pastoralists are found in:
q.x: The Masai are pastoralists of Kenya and Tanzania in East Africa.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of intensive subsistence farming?
q.x: Intensive subsistence farming relies on family labour on small plots, not heavy mechanisation.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a New World crop?
q.x: Sugarcane is an Old World crop (New Guinea/South Asia); maize, potato and tomato came from the Americas.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Columbian Exchange is correct?
o: It was the spice trade between India and Portugal.
It was the movement of crops between the Old and New Worlds after 1493.
It was the exchange of rice varieties within Asia.
It was a 19th-century trade treaty between Spain and Britain.
q.x: After Columbus, crops such as maize and potato moved to the Old World and sugarcane and coffee to the New.

q.s: Abadan, a major centre of oil refining, is located in:
q.x: Abadan is in Iran; Baku is the oil centre of Azerbaijan.

q.s: Anshan is an important iron and steel centre of:
q.x: Anshan in Liaoning is a major Chinese iron and steel centre.

q.s: Metz and Nancy are iron and steel centres of which region?
q.x: Metz and Nancy are in Lorraine, France.

q.s: Pittsburgh and Gary are centres of which steel region?
o: Great Lakes region of the USA
q.x: Pittsburgh and Gary belong to the Great Lakes steel region; Yawata is in Kitakyushu.

q.s: Which is the oldest industrial region of the USA?
q.x: New England is the oldest US industrial region.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an industrial centre of the Ruhr region?
q.x: Lyon is in France; Essen, Dortmund and Duisburg are Ruhr cities.

q.s: The Keihin industrial region of Japan is centred on:
q.x: Keihin is centred on Tokyo and Yokohama; Osaka and Kobe form Hanshin.

q.s: The Industrial Triangle of Northern Italy grew mainly on:
q.x: The Lombardy-Piedmont-Liguria triangle grew on Alpine hydroelectricity.

q.s: Magnitogorsk and Chelyabinsk are industrial centres of which region?
q.x: They are Ural centres; Kemerovo and Novokuznetsk are Kuzbass centres.

q.s: Under the Ural-Kuznetsk Combine, the Kuzbass sent to the Urals:
q.x: The Kuzbass sent coal to the Urals and received iron ore back.

q.s: Which country ranked first in new shipbuilding orders in 2025?
q.x: China ranked first, South Korea second (about 20%) and Japan third.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a labour-intensive industry?
q.x: Petroleum refining is capital-intensive; the others employ large numbers of workers.

q.s: Ambur and Ranipet, important leather clusters of India, are located in:
q.x: Ambur and Ranipet in the Vellore belt are Tamil Nadu leather clusters; Agra is in Uttar Pradesh.

q.s: Which country is the second-largest exporter of ready-made garments in the world after China?
q.x: Bangladesh is the second-largest garment exporter after China.

q.s: Etikoppaka toys of Andhra Pradesh, which hold a GI tag, are made in which district?
q.x: Etikoppaka toys are from Anakapalli district; Kondapalli toys are from NTR district.

q.s: Dharmavaram in Andhra Pradesh is famous for:
q.x: Dharmavaram (Sri Sathya Sai district) is a silk-saree centre.

q.s: Geoinformatics is an interdisciplinary field that combines geography with:
q.x: Geoinformatics combines geography and information technology.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a natural science?
q.x: Statistics is a formal science like mathematics.

q.s: The Indian School of Mines, Dhanbad, which became IIT (ISM) in 2016, was opened in the year:
q.x: ISM Dhanbad opened on 9 December 1926, modelled on the Royal School of Mines, London.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the scientific method is correct?
o: A well-tested theory finally becomes a law.
A theory is a well-tested explanation of why something happens.
A hypothesis is framed only after the theory is proved.
q.x: A theory explains why something happens; it never turns into a law, which only describes what happens.

q.s: Research that is driven by curiosity rather than by any immediate application is called:
q.x: Basic research is curiosity-driven; translational research is application-driven.

q.s: In a household electric circuit, a fuse is connected:
q.x: A fuse is connected in series; fuse wire has a low melting point and high resistivity.

q.s: A pressure cooker cooks food faster because it raises the boiling point of water to about:
q.x: Higher pressure raises the boiling point of water to about 120 °C.

q.s: A transformer works on:
q.x: A transformer works on electromagnetic induction and needs a changing current, so only on AC.

q.s: Wireless charging of mobile phones works on the principle of:
q.x: Wireless charging, like a dynamic microphone, works on electromagnetic induction.

q.s: One horsepower is equal to:
q.x: 1 horsepower = 746 W.

q.s: A light year is a unit of:
q.x: A light year is the distance light travels in one year.

q.s: Myopia (short-sightedness) is corrected by using a:
q.x: Myopia is corrected with a concave lens of negative power.

q.s: Which of the following does NOT use a convex lens?
q.x: Myopia is corrected with a concave lens.

q.s: If the momentum of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
q.x: KE = p²/2m, so doubling momentum makes KE four times.

q.s: A bird sitting on a single live high-voltage wire is safe because:
o: There is no potential difference across its body
q.x: Both feet are at the same potential, so no current flows through the bird.

q.s: Which is the second most abundant element in the Earth's crust?
q.x: Oxygen is first and silicon second in the Earth's crust.

q.s: Which state of matter is called the 'fourth state of matter'?
q.x: Plasma, an ionised gas, is the fourth state of matter.

q.s: Insulin, which lowers blood sugar, is secreted by which cells of the Islets of Langerhans?
q.x: Insulin comes from beta cells; glucagon, which raises blood sugar, from alpha cells.

q.s: Hydrochloric acid in the human stomach is secreted by the:
q.x: Parietal cells secrete HCl; chief cells secrete pepsinogen.

q.s: In cattle, the 'true stomach' where pepsin is produced is the:
q.x: Pepsin is made in the abomasum, the true stomach of ruminants.

q.s: The natural pacemaker of the human heart, the SA node, is located in the:
q.x: The SA node lies in the wall of the right atrium.

q.s: The ABO blood group system was discovered in 1901 by:
q.x: Karl Landsteiner discovered the ABO blood groups in 1901.

q.s: Temporary hardness of water is caused by the presence of:
q.x: Temporary hardness is due to bicarbonates of Ca and Mg and can be removed by boiling.

q.s: When baking soda reacts with vinegar, the gas released is:
q.x: Sodium bicarbonate and acetic acid release carbon dioxide.

q.s: Sodium metal is stored under kerosene because it:
o: Reacts violently with air and water
q.x: Sodium reacts vigorously with moisture and oxygen, so it is kept under kerosene.

q.s: The filament of an electric bulb is made of tungsten because tungsten has a very high:
q.x: Tungsten's very high melting point lets it glow without melting; nichrome is used for heater coils.

q.s: The purity of 22 carat gold is about:
q.x: 22 carat gold is 22/24 = 91.6% pure; 18 carat is 75%.

q.s: Aqua regia is a mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and nitric acid in the ratio:
q.x: Aqua regia is HCl and HNO3 in the ratio 3 : 1.

q.s: Which of the following vitamins is NOT fat-soluble?
q.x: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble; vitamin C is water-soluble.

q.s: Cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) contains which metal?
q.x: Vitamin B12 contains cobalt.

q.s: The term 'vitamine' was coined in 1912 by:
q.x: Casimir Funk coined 'vitamine' in 1912.

q.s: The anti-beriberi substance 'aberic acid' extracted from rice bran by Umetaro Suzuki was later identified as:
q.x: Suzuki's aberic acid was vitamin B1.

q.s: Which of the following has the highest protein content (about 40 g per 100 g)?
q.x: Soybean has about 40 g protein per 100 g, the highest among grains and pulses.

q.s: Proteins provide about how much energy per gram?
q.x: Proteins and carbohydrates give about 4 kcal per gram; fat about 9 kcal.

q.s: Which is the sweetest natural sugar?
q.x: Fructose is the sweetest natural sugar.

q.s: Which nutrient gives the most energy per gram (about 9 kcal)?
q.x: Fat gives about 9 kcal per gram; carbohydrates and proteins about 4 kcal.

q.s: The '+F' logo of FSSAI is used to identify:
q.x: FSSAI's '+F' logo marks fortified food.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an artificial sweetener?
q.x: Fructose is a natural fruit sugar.

q.s: Adulteration of mustard oil with argemone oil causes:
q.x: Argemone oil causes epidemic dropsy; lathyrism is from Khesari dal.

q.s: Turmeric is commonly adulterated with:
q.x: Turmeric is adulterated with metanil yellow and lead chromate; Rhodamine B is used in cotton candy.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a negative impact of technology on daily life?
q.x: Flexible work is a positive impact; the others are negative.

q.s: The photoelectric effect was discovered by:
q.x: Hertz discovered the photoelectric effect (1887); Einstein explained it.

q.s: Electricity and magnetism were unified into the theory of electromagnetism by:
q.x: Maxwell's equations unified electricity and magnetism.

q.s: C.V. Raman discovered the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928 while working at:
q.x: Raman worked at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS), Calcutta.

q.s: C.V. Raman was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in the year:
q.x: Raman was knighted in 1929, won the Nobel in 1930 and the Bharat Ratna in 1954.

q.s: The Bose Institute, Kolkata was founded by J.C. Bose in the year:
q.x: Bose Institute was founded in 1917; Indian Academy of Sciences 1934; TIFR 1945.

q.s: The Raman Research Institute, Bengaluru was founded in the year:
q.x: C.V. Raman founded the RRI in 1948.

q.s: 'Bhabha scattering' refers to scattering between:
q.x: Bhabha scattering is electron-positron scattering.

q.s: The Adams Prize, received by Homi Bhabha in 1942, is awarded by:
q.x: The Adams Prize is awarded by Cambridge University.

q.s: National Mathematics Day, observed on 22 December, marks the birth anniversary of:
q.x: 22 December is Ramanujan's birthday; National Science Day (28 February) marks the Raman Effect.

q.s: The number 1729 is popularly known as the:
q.x: 1729 is the Hardy-Ramanujan number; Kaprekar's constant is 6174.

q.s: S.N. Bose's 1924 paper 'Planck's Law and the Hypothesis of Light Quanta' was translated into German by:
q.x: Einstein translated and published Bose's paper, leading to Bose-Einstein statistics.

q.s: Rabindranath Tagore dedicated his book 'Visva-Parichay' to:
q.x: Tagore dedicated Visva-Parichay to S.N. Bose.

q.s: The Saha ionisation equation, given by Meghnad Saha, is a basic tool for studying:
q.x: The Saha equation is used to interpret stellar spectra.

q.s: Meghnad Saha prepared the original plan for which river valley project?
q.x: Saha prepared the original plan of the Damodar Valley Project.

q.s: Kamala Sohonie, the first Indian woman to earn a PhD in a science discipline (1939), received it from:
q.x: Her PhD was from Cambridge; she was also the first woman admitted to IISc.

q.s: The anti-epileptic drug Ayush-56 was developed by:
q.x: Asima Chatterjee developed Ayush-56; she was also the first woman General President of the Indian Science Congress (1975).

q.s: Which Indian scientist is known as the 'Weather Woman of India'?
q.x: Anna Mani is called the Weather Woman of India.

q.s: The Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS), Kolkata, was founded in 1876 by:
q.x: Mahendra Lal Sircar founded IACS in 1876.

q.s: The Radio Astronomy Centre at Ooty is run by:
q.x: The Ooty Radio Astronomy Centre is run by TIFR.

q.s: The Crescograph, an instrument to measure plant growth, was invented by:
q.x: J.C. Bose invented the Crescograph and wrote 'Response in the Living and Non-Living' (1902).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with Jagadish Chandra Bose?
o: Use of the coherer and galena detector in radio research
q.x: The Raman Effect was discovered by C.V. Raman.

q.s: Who co-authored A.P.J. Abdul Kalam's autobiography 'Wings of Fire' (1999)?
q.x: Kalam wrote 'Wings of Fire' with Arun Tiwari.

q.s: In 2006, A.P.J. Abdul Kalam became the first Indian Head of State to fly in which fighter aircraft?
q.x: Kalam flew in a Sukhoi-30 MKI in 2006; Pratibha Patil flew in one in 2009.

q.s: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan shared the 2009 Nobel Prize for the structure of the ribosome in the field of:
q.x: Ramakrishnan's 2009 Nobel was in Chemistry.

q.s: Har Gobind Khorana shared the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with:
q.x: Khorana shared it with Robert Holley and Marshall Nirenberg; he also made the first synthetic gene.

q.s: Which of the following scientists was NOT a Bharat Ratna awardee?
q.x: Kalam (1997), C.N.R. Rao (2014) and M.S. Swaminathan (2024) received the Bharat Ratna; Bhabha received the Padma Bhushan.

q.s: Yellapragada SubbaRow, the scientist from Andhra Pradesh, is associated with the development of:
q.x: SubbaRow is linked with folic acid, methotrexate and the Fiske-SubbaRow method for ATP and phosphocreatine.

q.s: Yelavarthy Nayudamma of Guntur, who died in the Kanishka bombing of 1985, headed which institution?
q.x: Nayudamma was director of the Central Leather Research Institute (CLRI), Chennai.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an operating system?
q.x: Microsoft Office is application software, not an operating system.

q.s: The UNIX operating system was developed in 1969 at:
q.x: UNIX was developed at AT&T's Bell Labs in 1969.

q.s: An operating system with fixed response deadlines, used in missile guidance and air-traffic control, is a:
q.x: A real-time OS guarantees responses within fixed deadlines.

q.s: Cache memory in a computer is usually made of:
q.x: Cache is SRAM; DRAM is used for main memory.

q.s: The BIOS of a computer is stored in:
q.x: BIOS is held in ROM (now flash/EEPROM) so it survives power-off.

q.s: Magnetic tape, the slowest form of secondary storage, provides which type of data access?
q.x: Magnetic tape is sequential-access.

q.s: EPROM (Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory) is erased by:
q.x: EPROM is erased by UV light; EEPROM is erased electrically.

q.s: A Solid State Drive (SSD) stores data using:
q.x: An SSD uses flash memory and has no moving parts.

q.s: In computing, a 'nibble' is equal to:
q.x: A nibble is 4 bits, half a byte.

q.s: Which of the following statements about computer units is correct?
o: A picosecond is shorter than a nanosecond.
q.x: A picosecond (10^-12 s) is shorter than a nanosecond (10^-9 s); a nibble is 4 bits and 1 TB is 1024 GB.

q.s: Which of the following are known as universal logic gates?
q.x: NAND and NOR are universal gates; any logic circuit can be built from either.

q.s: An XOR gate gives an output of 1 when:
q.x: XOR gives 1 only when its inputs differ.

q.s: Which was the first high-level programming language, developed by IBM in 1957?
q.x: FORTRAN (IBM, 1957) was the first high-level language.

q.s: Which of the following programming languages is NOT mainly associated with artificial intelligence?
q.x: COBOL is a business data-processing language; PROLOG and LISP are classic AI languages.

q.s: The SMPS (Switched Mode Power Supply) in a computer converts:
q.x: An SMPS converts mains AC into the low-voltage DC used by computer parts.

q.s: Third-generation computers were based on:
q.x: Third-generation computers used ICs; transistors marked the second and VLSI/microprocessors the fourth.

q.s: Which of the following statements about computer generations is correct?
o: Fourth-generation computers were based on VLSI and microprocessors.
q.x: The sequence is vacuum tubes, transistors, ICs, then VLSI/microprocessors; AI and ULSI mark the fifth.

q.s: The Linux kernel was written in 1991 by:
q.x: Linus Torvalds wrote the Linux kernel; Stallman founded the GNU Project.

q.s: The Java programming language was created by:
q.x: James Gosling created Java; Stroustrup created C++.

q.s: Which of the following is an example of a device that works as both an input and an output device?
q.x: A touch screen takes input and displays output; a laser printer is a non-impact output device.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an impact printer?
q.x: A laser printer is a non-impact printer.

q.s: PARAM Padma, an Indian supercomputer, was built by:
q.x: PARAM series supercomputers are built by C-DAC.

q.s: Patient monitors in an ICU, which combine analog and digital features, are examples of:
q.x: ICU monitors are hybrid computers.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the World Wide Web is correct?
o: The deep web is fully indexed by search engines.
The surface web forms about 90% of the Web.
Web 3.0 consists of static, read-only HTML pages.
The dark web is a small hidden part of the deep web reached with tools such as Tor.
q.x: The dark web is a small part of the deep web (90-95% of the Web, unindexed); static read-only pages describe Web 1.0.

q.s: In the OSI model, TCP and UDP operate at the:
q.x: TCP and UDP are Transport layer (layer 4) protocols.

q.s: Encryption, compression and data formatting are functions of which OSI layer?
q.x: These are Presentation layer functions.

q.s: How many layers does the OSI reference model have?
q.x: The OSI model has seven layers, with Application at the top and Physical at the bottom.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a layer of the OSI model?
q.x: The Internet layer belongs to the TCP/IP model, not the OSI model.

q.s: Which protocol is used for sending e-mail?
q.x: SMTP sends mail; POP3 and IMAP receive it.

q.s: Which e-mail protocol keeps mail on the server and synchronised across devices?
q.x: IMAP keeps mail synced on the server; POP3 downloads it to one device.

q.s: A company linking its LANs in Mumbai, Bengaluru and New Delhi uses a:
q.x: Networks spread across cities are WANs.

q.s: Ethernet, the common LAN technology, follows the standard:
q.x: Ethernet is IEEE 802.3; Wi-Fi is 802.11 and Bluetooth 802.15.1.

q.s: Which network topology is the most resilient, needing n(n-1)/2 links for n nodes?
q.x: A full mesh links every node to every other node.

q.s: In a star topology, the failure of which component stops the whole network?
q.x: In a star, the failure of the hub stops the network; a node's failure affects only that node.

q.s: An IPv6 address is how many bits long?
q.x: IPv6 is 128 bits; IPv4 is 32 bits and a MAC address 48 bits.

q.s: A MAC address is how many bits long?
q.x: A MAC address is 48 bits.

q.s: Wi-Fi networks follow which IEEE standard?
q.x: Wi-Fi follows IEEE 802.11; Bluetooth follows 802.15.1.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Bluetooth is correct?
o: It needs line of sight between devices.
It transmits data using light waves.
q.x: Bluetooth uses 2.4 GHz radio waves (IEEE 802.15.1) and needs no line of sight.

q.s: Li-Fi technology transmits data using:
q.x: Li-Fi carries data on visible light from LEDs.

q.s: Wi-Fi 6 corresponds to which IEEE standard?
q.x: Wi-Fi 6 is 802.11ax; Wi-Fi 7 is 802.11be.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of multimedia?
q.x: Multimedia combines text, graphics, audio, video and animation; a compiler is system software.

q.s: DD Free Dish, India's first free DTH service, was launched in:
q.x: DD Free Dish began in December 2004.

q.s: DTH (Direct-to-Home) television receives its signals from:
q.x: DTH takes signals from geostationary satellites straight to home dishes.

q.s: The approximate working range of Near Field Communication (NFC) is about:
q.x: NFC works over only a few centimetres, much less than Bluetooth.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Near Field Communication (NFC) is correct?
o: It has a longer range than Bluetooth.
It cannot be used for UPI payments.
It uses less power than Bluetooth.
q.x: NFC uses radio fields over a few centimetres, needs less power than Bluetooth, and supports offline UPI Lite payments.

q.s: In the e-mail address mark.sttol@ITdesk.info, the domain name is:
q.x: The part after '@' is the domain; mark.sttol is the user name.

q.s: Which e-mail field sends a copy while hiding that recipient's address from other recipients?
q.x: BCC (blind carbon copy) hides recipients' addresses from one another.

q.s: 'Nomophobia' refers to:
o: Fear of being without one's mobile phone
q.x: Nomophobia is 'no-mobile-phone phobia'.

q.s: Gaming Disorder has been included in which WHO classification?
q.x: Gaming Disorder is listed in the WHO's ICD-11.

q.s: Which of the following statements about waves is correct?
o: Sound is a mechanical, longitudinal wave.
Sound travels faster in air than in steel.
X-rays are deflected by magnetic fields.
Sound can travel through a vacuum.
q.x: Sound is a mechanical longitudinal wave, faster in solids than in air; X-rays are uncharged and not deflected.

q.s: In an electrochemical cell, oxidation takes place at the:
q.x: Oxidation occurs at the anode and reduction (gain of electrons) at the cathode.

q.s: In electrochemistry, reduction means:
q.x: Reduction is gain of electrons and takes place at the cathode.

q.s: The use of Ni-Cd batteries is declining mainly because:
q.x: Cadmium is toxic, so Ni-Cd cells are being phased out.

q.s: Which of the following batteries is NOT rechargeable?
q.x: The zinc-carbon dry cell used in torches is a primary, non-rechargeable cell.

q.s: The enzyme bromelain is obtained from:
q.x: Bromelain comes from pineapple; papain from papaya.

q.s: Which of the following is an animal protease, NOT a plant protease?
q.x: Trypsin is a pancreatic (animal) protease; papain, bromelain and ficin are from plants.

q.s: The technique of DNA fingerprinting was developed in 1984 by:
q.x: Alec Jeffreys developed DNA fingerprinting; Lalji Singh pioneered it in India.

q.s: The Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics (CDFD) is located at:
q.x: CDFD is in Hyderabad.

q.s: Graphite is soft and slippery because its layers are held together by:
q.x: Graphite's layers are held by weak van der Waals forces and slide over each other.

q.s: Which of the following statements about forms of carbon is correct?
o: Graphite is transparent with a very high refractive index.
Diamond is a good conductor of electricity.
Graphite layers are joined by strong ionic bonds.
Activated charcoal is porous with a very high surface area.
q.x: Activated charcoal's porosity gives a huge surface area; transparency and high refractive index belong to diamond.

q.s: Which blood group is the universal donor for plasma?
q.x: AB plasma has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, so AB is the universal plasma donor.

q.s: Which blood group is known as the universal recipient?
q.x: AB positive has no anti-A, anti-B or anti-Rh antibodies.
